Unique elements of an array

Source: R/numpy_setops.R
jnp_unique.Rd

Port of jnp.unique and of the array API functions jnp.unique_all, jnp.unique_counts, jnp.unique_inverse and jnp.unique_values. Without size the input must be concrete (outside of jit); with a static size the result has exactly size entries along the unique axis, padded with fill_value (by default the smallest unique value) or truncated.

Usage

jnp_unique(
  ar,
  return_index = FALSE,
  return_inverse = FALSE,
  return_counts = FALSE,
  axis = NULL,
  equal_nan = TRUE,
  size = NULL,
  fill_value = NULL,
  sorted = TRUE
)

jnp_unique_all(x, size = NULL, fill_value = NULL)

jnp_unique_counts(x, size = NULL, fill_value = NULL)

jnp_unique_inverse(x, size = NULL, fill_value = NULL)

jnp_unique_values(x, size = NULL, fill_value = NULL)

Arguments

ar, x

Array.

return_index

Also return the 0-based indices of the first occurrences.

return_inverse

Also return the indices that rebuild ar from the result.

return_counts

Also return the number of occurrences of each unique value.

axis

0-based axis along which to find unique slices; NULL flattens.

equal_nan

Treat all NaN values as equal.

size

Optional static number of unique values to return.

fill_value

Padding value when size exceeds the number of unique values.

sorted

Ignored (results are always sorted).

Value

An array, or a list of arrays when any return_* flag is set. unique_all, unique_counts and unique_inverse return named lists with the fields values, indices, inverse_indices and counts.
